turns.content: @all I've been going back and reprocessing my Orion image from November for the hundredth time and it still looks flat compared to Jerome's work. Is there any chance you'd walk me through how you actually blend it?? 🙏📷

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.content: the Ha-RGB blend is not complicated once you understand what you are doing, but there are three things most people get wrong that kill the result. first: your Ha data needs to be calibrated and stacked separately, not mixed in during the initial integration. second: in PixInsight you use the ChannelCombination process with Ha mapped to the red channel of a synthetic luminance, then combine with a Luminance mask to protect star colours. third, and this is where most broadband imagers fail: you need to apply a Hue-Saturation adjustment after the blend to desaturate the magenta cast that appears in the red-blue transition zones around HII regions. if you skip that step your stars look radioactive and the nebula looks like a bad Instagram filter. send me your Orion FITS stack and I will step through it with you here in the chat.

turns.speaker: Cecilia
turns.content: ok sending the FITS now. and I have to ask... I always thought narrowband looked really cold and mono, like it strips all the warmth out. is there a way to keep the broadband colour and just add the Ha detail on top? 📷

turns.speaker: Jerome
turns.content: that is exactly what the Ha-RGB blend does. you keep the full broadband RGB as your colour base and add the Ha emission only where it contributes signal. the PixInsight workflow I use is: LinearFit both datasets to match background levels, then use PixelMath with the expression: Ha_weight multiplied by Ha plus open-bracket 1 minus Ha_weight close-bracket multiplied by R, where Ha_weight is typically 0.7. you replace the red channel with this blended value and recombine. the result is your broadband warmth with Ha emission boosting the ionised hydrogen regions. it is the best of both methods technically speaking. try it on the Orion core and tell me if the Trapezium halo structure changes.
